narrative.overview:
Digix is opened rarely, so its screens read at a glance and then get out of the way. The look is user-pinned: Apple-style and simple, in the manner of shadcn. Apple supplies the large titles, pinned navigation bar, stretching switch and push transitions. shadcn supplies the zinc scale, hairline groups and near-black buttons. Density is relaxed but compact: one column of bordered rows on a near-white or near-black ground.

Restraint is the identity and motion carries the delight. Surfaces stay flat and uncoloured at rest. When something happens, a spring moves it and a haptic confirms it. The single authored element is the line-drawn watch in onboarding, which persists across every step and reacts to a real dial. The rejected directions are themed concepts, skeuomorphism, gradients and decorated cards.

Theming follows the system light or dark setting. There is no Material You dynamic colour and no in-app theme choice. Material 3 is present only as plumbing: its colour scheme, `Text`, `Icon` and ripple. Every control is drawn by the app.
keyCharacteristics: Zinc neutrals with an inverting near-black or near-white primary, and no brand hue.
One green, which only ever means live or just ran.
Inter alone, at two optical sizes, with strong weight contrast and tabular codes.
1dp hairlines and tonal tiles instead of shadows.
Springs on movement, scale, size and colour, paired with a small haptic vocabulary.
Sentence case everywhere. Nothing is uppercase, and there are no kickers or eyebrows.

rules.name: The One Green Rule
rules.body: Green means Digix is listening or a code really ran, and nothing else. Buttons, links, ordinary switches and setup checks stay neutral, which is why the Haptics switch and the finished step mark use the primary colour.

rules.name: The No-Brand-Hue Rule
rules.body: The primary action is ink on paper. Emphasis comes from inversion and weight, never from a coloured accent.

rules.name: The Two-Signals Rule
rules.body: No state is carried by colour alone. On and off pair the word with a filled or hollow dot and the switch position, a needs-setup row says so in words, and an error is a sentence.

rules.name: The Tabular Code Rule
rules.body: A code always renders in Code or Code Large and always reads left to right, including in right-to-left languages. TalkBack hears it digit by digit.

rules.name: The Tracking Gate Rule
rules.body: Negative tracking applies only to Latin-like scripts. The theme switches it to zero for Arabic, Hebrew, Indic and Southeast Asian languages, because tightening damages those scripts. Positive tracking on numerals is not gated.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Separation is a hairline or an opaque ground. A floating element gets both, and never a shadow.

rules.name: The Earned Bounce Rule
rules.body: Visible overshoot belongs to the moments of arrival: the check landing and the onboarding watch. Everything else settles without bounce.

rules.name: The Signature Haptic Rule
rules.body: `codeCaught`, a quick rise followed by a click 40ms later, plays only when a code from the watch really ran. No other event may use it.

dos: Do put new content in a Group: a 1dp hairline at the 12dp radius, with no fill at rest.
Do start every app screen with the Pinned Bar and Large Title, inside the 16dp gutter.
Do pair a state change with a spring from the theme and a haptic from the vocabulary.
Do give every state a word as well as a colour or shape.
Do use Inverting Ink for one primary action per view, and outline or ghost for the rest.
Do render codes in Code or Code Large, forced left to right.
Do check the removed-animations setting for anything that loops or scales under the finger.
Do keep status colours on text and marks, and use them only when there is something to report.
donts: Don't use Live Green for anything except listening or a code that really ran.
Don't add shadows, elevation or gradients.
Don't add themed concepts or skeuomorphic detail. The flat line-drawn watch is the one illustration.
Don't add a second typeface or a monospace for codes.
Don't set text in uppercase or add kickers above headings.
Don't add a radius beyond 12dp, 8dp and fully round.
Don't use Material chrome such as buttons, switches, cards, top bars or dialogs. Draw the control from these tokens.
Don't tween movement or scale. Tweens are for opacity and ambient loops.
Don't celebrate before the result is real. The green check and `codeCaught` follow a completed run.
notCanonized: The white thumb on the dark theme's live track is 2.28:1, under the 3:1 non-text guideline. The light theme is 3.3:1. Position, dot and word also carry this state.
The hairline is 1.22:1 on the light ground and 1.34:1 on the dark ground, so it is a separator and not a sufficient boundary alone. Outlined controls here rely on a label or value inside them.
Section gaps vary between 18, 22, 26 and 28dp with no shared constant, and the title scroll threshold is a raw 90px rather than dp.
The theme's comment and the direction contract both say springs drive every state change, while opacity uses tweens. This file records the build.
The `caption` type style, the Code Badge `highlighted` state and the 700 weight instance exist in code and are unused, so they are left out of this system.
